title: Unmanaged privileged access
scenario: An attacker compromises a privileged account and deploys ransomware across critical systems.
csf_category: PR.AA — Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control
existing_controls: MFA on selected systems; periodic access reviews
recommended_treatment: Enforce phishing-resistant MFA for administrators; use PAM/JIT elevation; review privileged access quarterly.

title: Phishing and credential theft
scenario: A user follows a malicious link or opens a weaponized attachment, enabling credential theft and initial access.
csf_category: PR.AT — Awareness and Training; PR.DS — Data Security
recommended_treatment: Run role-based phishing exercises; improve email authentication and attachment detonation; use conditional access.

title: Insufficient endpoint detection
scenario: Ransomware executes on an endpoint without timely alerting, allowing lateral movement and encryption.
recommended_treatment: Deploy centrally monitored EDR to servers and endpoints; tune detections; test alert escalation and coverage.

title: Excessive network reachability
scenario: An attacker moves laterally from a compromised workstation to server and backup networks.
existing_controls: Core firewall rules; some network segmentation
recommended_treatment: Segment user, server, identity, and backup networks; restrict east-west traffic; review rules and remote access.

title: Backups exposed to ransomware
scenario: Attackers delete or encrypt online backups, preventing timely restoration after a ransomware incident.
recommended_treatment: Maintain immutable/offline copies; isolate backup credentials; test clean restores and recovery time objectives.

title: Unverified incident response readiness
scenario: Teams lack a practiced ransomware playbook, delaying containment, communications, and recovery decisions.
recommended_treatment: Create a ransomware playbook with legal, privacy, communications, IT, and executive roles; conduct tabletop exercises.

title: Critical asset inventory gaps
scenario: An unknown or unsupported asset remains unpatched and becomes an entry point for ransomware.
recommended_treatment: Reconcile endpoint, cloud, identity, and OT/IoT inventories; assign business criticality and system owners.

title: Weak third-party access governance
scenario: A compromised supplier account or remote management tool is used to access enterprise systems.
csf_category: GV.SC — Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
recommended_treatment: Inventory critical suppliers; constrain vendor access; require MFA, time-bound approvals, logging, and incident notice terms.

title: Delayed vulnerability remediation
scenario: An exploitable internet-facing or high-value system remains vulnerable and is used for initial access.
recommended_treatment: Prioritize remediation by exploitability and asset criticality; define SLAs; verify closure through rescanning.

title: Recovery dependencies not validated
scenario: Restoration fails because identity, DNS, certificates, or clean build dependencies are unavailable.
existing_controls: Documented recovery steps for selected services
recommended_treatment: Map service dependencies; maintain clean recovery credentials and golden images; test recovery in an isolated environment.
